Sources indicate that a, A detailed schematic of the workflow is shown: (i) Matrigel is microcontact printed onto the two-layered PDMS stamp (PDMS-ii) using a flat PDMS stamp (PDMS-i). (ii) A thin PDMS microwell array is peeled from the silicon master and overlaid on a glass coverslip. Taller PDMS sidewalls are plasma-bonded along two edges. (iii) Capillary water flow through the microchannels drives localized Matrigel transfer from stamp PDMS-ii onto the PDMS microwell layer at the contact interface. (iv) Cells are seeded onto the transferred Matrigel pattern, overlaid with a silanized coverslip atop the sidewalls, and cultured further with media and microwell-trapped beads. b, Photographs of the experimental setup corresponding to steps a(i–iii): coating the flat stamp (grey border, fourth column, top); PDMS-ii stamps with different patterns (blue border, first column); PDMS microwell layer with wells at different positions (red border, second column); aligned PDMS-ii stamp and PDMS microwell layer in contact (green border, third column); and the application of weight and water flow for transfer (green border, fourth column, bottom). It has been revealed that a, A schematic of trunk morph differentiation protocol is shown. hPSCs were seeded onto micropatterned PDMS microwell substrate on Day −3 in mTeSR Plus with 10 µM Y-27632. On Day 0, BMP4-coated beads were injected into microwells, and cyst differentiation was initiated in N2B27 with 8–10 µM CHIR99021, 0.1–0.15 µM A83-01, and 50 ng ml−1 NOGGIN. After 48 h, cysts were transferred to individual wells in N2B27 with Matrigel and cultured for 3–4 days before analysis. b, Box-and-whisker plots show length of trunk morphs at 0, 48, and 120 h of differentiation. The same n = 93 biologically independent trunk morph samples were tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. c, (left) Box-and-whisker plots of trunk morph length on days 3, 4 and 5 without (red, n = 10 biologically independent trunk morph samples) or with the WNT-secretion inhibitor IWP3 (green, n = 8 biologically independent trunk morph samples), added after 48 h; each morph was tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. Differences between conditions at each time point were assessed using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons; Hodges-Lehmann median differences are given with Bonferroni-adjusted (98.3%) confidence intervals. Day 3: U = 16, P = 0.103, −59 µm (−160 to 18). Day 4: U = 4, P = 1.6 × 10−3, −212 µm (−314 to −100). Day 5: U = 0, P = 1.4 × 10−4, −353 µm (−438 to −287). ns, P > 0.05; **, P < 0.01; ***, P < 0.001. Nicky Devlin has predicted that Findlay Marshall will continue to sparkle if he’s played at the top of Aberdeen’s diamond formation.

On the back of netting his first senior goal for the Dons from the bench against Kilmarnock, new boss Mario Frick deployed the 20-year-old from the start against Rangers in a central attacking role.

In what proved to be a man of the match display, Marshall set up Brad Lyons’ opener then claimed a goal of his own with a sweet left-foot finish.

And with Frick seemingly intent on sticking with the blueprint which caused Killie and Rangers problems, defender Devlin believes his younger team-mate, who enjoyed a successful loan spell at Arbroath last season, will only go from strength to strength.

According to recent reports, ‘Even at Arbroath, you saw how much of a goal threat he is,’ said Devlin. ‘He makes really good runs into the box and off both feet he’s a really good finisher.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He can definitely play other roles, especially in the formation that the manager’s been playing just now. But I think you get the best out of him when you let him attack the box, let him get into the box to score goals.

Industry observers note that ‘For me, he was the best player on the park. Especially for someone so young, to go there... he’ll probably hate me for saying it, but I could tell he was maybe a wee bit nervous because he told me about three or four times that it’s the first time he’d ever been to Ibrox.

Findlay Marshall in the thick of the action against Rangers in this week's 3-2 loss for Dons.

According to recent reports, ‘So, I knew he was thinking about it. But then he goes and delivers a performance like that.

It has been revealed that ‘His finishing, especially off his left foot, is unbelievable. He could easily have got us a draw. He was really unlucky with an effort right at the end.

‘He’s grown so much, especially since I came to the club at first. He’s an example for everyone at our club in terms of youth players. He’s gone and done what the club wanted him to do. He’s had two or three different loans where he’s gone away, played well, scored goals, came back, had to wait his opportunity.

‘In the last two games that he’s come in, he’s scored two goals and he’s been brilliant.’.

Marshall’s first goal for the Dons at Rugby Park was another crisp left-foot finish which came when he decided not to play in a team-mate.

Devlin feels that the better decision-making he’s now showing is a sign that his game is starting to click into place.

In a recent development, ‘He’s a younger boy who just wants to learn all the time,’ he explained. ‘He mentioned after the game on Saturday that he had a chance like that in the cup and he chose the other option. He tried to play in maybe the more senior player just because he thought that was the right thing to do. He took on board that he should have maybe gone himself.

Sources indicate that ‘It was an unbelievable finish. That’s what he brings to the team. That’s what he can bring to us. And hopefully he can keep doing that.’.

Marshall is only 20 but was Aberdeen's star man in the match at Ibrox on Tuesday night.

Born in Stonehaven and part of the Dons’ set-up since 2017, Marshall is the new poster boy for the club.

At a time when the opportunities being afforded to young Scots is a hot topic, Devlin feels that Aberdeen have much to feel optimistic about on that score.

‘I think we’ve got plenty here that I think can definitely step up and come in,’ he explained.

‘You see towards the end of the game, we’re chasing a goal with 20 minutes to go and the manager turns to a 15-year-old (Andrew Fasanya). So, there’s players there that can come through.

According to recent reports, ‘There’s a few boys out on loan now that are doing excellent. The two Alfies at Inverness (Bavidge and Stewart) and Dylan Lobban has done brilliant at Dunfermline.

‘So, there’s definitely players there that can step up for us. Hopefully, they’ll get their opportunity through time. But I’m pretty sure the manager’s trying to assess everyone in the squad just now.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tuttomercato carries Luciano Spalletti’s reaction to the talk linking Weston McKennie with Manchester United, and the Juventus head coach played it down.
  • Those comments came from McKennie himself, who suggested during USMNT camp that Mauricio Pochettino could bring American players to Old Trafford.
  • Pochettino inherits a club in trouble: one win and eight points from ten league games, 18th place and Michael Carrick’s sacking after their worst league start in 40 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tuttomercato carries Luciano Spalletti’s reaction to the talk linking Weston McKennie with Manchester United, and the Juventus head coach played it down. He spoke to the midfielder as soon as the story broke and didn’t think McKennie had hinted at wanting to leave, calling his comments a general remark. Spalletti stated their relationship is as good as the one he has with everybody else, and everything felt calm once McKennie returned from international duty.

Those comments came from McKennie himself, who suggested during USMNT camp that Mauricio Pochettino could bring American players to Old Trafford. La Gazzetta dello Sport then reported that United’s latest head coach wants him in January, though McKennie says he isn’t planning to leave and Fabrizio Romano insists United aren’t working on a deal.

Pochettino inherits a club in trouble: one win and eight points from ten league games, 18th place and Michael Carrick’s sacking after their worst league start in 40 years. The Argentine takes charge at Anfield today, before Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Sporting CP.

According to recent reports, mcKennie, 28, offers versatility: Spalletti has used him on both wings, at wing-back and even as a striker, and he managed eight goals and five assists in 38 appearances before signing his new deal in March. This season the output has dipped, with FotMob showing one goal, no assists and a 6.98 rating from eight Serie A starts. His contract runs to 2030, and FotMob values him at about £28m.

Not as a January priority. United’s problem is a team that loses control of matches, and McKennie is a runner who arrives in the box rather than a midfielder who dictates tempo. Put him next to a struggling back four and his versatility becomes a drawback, because Spalletti gets the best from him higher up the pitch, where his goals come from.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

Romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • According to recent reports, juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • Sources indicate that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

According to recent reports, juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

Sources indicate that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the latest refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

Sources indicate that the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

According to recent reports, the case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

According to recent reports, close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

Recent findings suggest that the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

Industry observers note that the first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:33.

Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.

Moreirense spent much of the previous campaign in contention for a European place but eventually finished seventh, and they are at the moment some way off the pace in the race for a top-five finish following an inconsistent start to this season.

Vasco Botelho da Costa's men have won just four of their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L5), while struggling at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 18, the weakest defensive record among the current top-half sides.

The Moreira-based club enter this encounter on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon, which ended a two-match winning run following victories over Estoril Praia and Estrela Amadora.

Although losing by a single goal away to Sporting is hardly the most disappointing result, Da Costa will be concerned by a pattern that has seen his side suffer their last three defeats by the same 1-0 scoreline, including a Taca de Portugal exit at the hands of second-tier AVS.

Moreirense have also struggled for consistency on home soil this season, winning just two of their five league matches at Parque Moreira de Conegos (D1, L2), although a 2-1 victory over Estrela in their most recent outing at the venue gives them an opportunity to secure consecutive home wins for the first time since April and May.

Santa Clara, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to the Primeira Liga campaign, collecting 21 points from their opening 11 matches (W6, D3, L2), although Petit's side have recently seen the resilience that characterised their early-season performances begin to fade.

After going unbeaten in their first eight fixtures (W5, D3), the Azoreans have lost three of their last four competitive outings, beginning with a disappointing Taca de Portugal exit against lower-division Mafra before suffering a league defeat to Benfica.

Although they bounced back with a victory away to Maritimo, Santa Clara were beaten 2-1 by Gil Vicente in their most recent top-flight outing before playing out a 2-2 draw against Valladolid in a friendly on November 11.

Nevertheless, Petit's men remain among the hardest sides to break down in the division, having conceded just eight league goals, with only leaders Porto (five) boasting a better defensive record, while Santa Clara have scored twice as many at the other end.

Their away performances have been particularly impressive, with the Azoreans collecting 13 points from five league trips (W4, D1), giving them the third-best away record in this season's Primeira Liga behind Porto and Benfica.

However, the visitors have struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last four league meetings with Moreirense and losing three, including both encounters last season, which ended in 1-0 defeats.

Moreirense will welcome Tiago Andrade back into contention after the winger recovered from the muscle problem that ruled him out of the trip to Sporting.

Meanwhile, Alexandre Parsemain (leg) and Joao Veloso (muscle) remain doubts, while Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso are still recovering from their respective muscle injuries and are expected to remain unavailable.

With Parsemain's availability uncertain, Leonardo Vonic could lead the line once again, although Yan Maranho is another option in that position.

Santa Clara have considerably greater selection problems, with first-choice centre-backs Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira both suspended following their disciplinary complications against Gil Vicente, with the former receiving a red card and the latter missing out through an accumulation of bookings.

Petit's defensive options are further limited by the potential absence of Guilherme Romao, who is sidelined with injury, though Pedro Ferreira could return this weekend if he is fully fit following a nose matter.

As a result, Ythallo could make his senior debut alongside Henrique Silva in central defence, although both have limited first-team experience, having featured predominantly at youth level and as a substitute, respectively.

Goncalo Paciencia returned from injury as a second-half substitute last time out and could lead the line here, potentially leaving Fernando to make way.

There is also good  news in goal,  with Lucas Franca having recovered from a muscle injury and expected to return to contention for the starting role.

A Ferreira; Pinto, Kevyn Monteiro, Batista, A Martinez; N John, Liberato; Andrade, Mendonca, Landerson; Vonic.

Santa Clara possible starting lineup:.

Franca; Lucas Soares, Ythallo, H Silva, Fofana; Tavares, Borges, Vasconcelos; V Lopes, Paciencia, B Lucas.

Santa Clara have been considerably stronger away from home this season, but their defensive absences could prove costly against a Moreirense side that have won three of the last four meetings between the clubs.

Furthermore, the hosts have an opportunity to exploit an inexperienced centre-back pairing, although their own scoring problems and the visitors' impressive away record suggest neither side will have enough to claim all three points.

#209347. Breaking: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1165 w)

Breaking: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1165 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

Recent findings suggest that the plate and the photos are on show at the latest exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, indicates exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Alongside Picasso, a surprising number of crucial artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

It has been revealed that two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to glitch a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

In a recent development, however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

Industry observers note that the dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked massive and dangerous.".

Industry observers note that the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian states. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a latest image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

The designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

But altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

The feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

Recent findings suggest that "It's really crazy," she states, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January.
  • In a recent development, calhanoglu turns 33 in February.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

According to recent reports, the timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

In a recent development, calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob highlights three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

It has been revealed that passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

Roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:49.

Coming off a three-week break from competitive action, Academico de Viseu and Alverca meet at Estadio do Fontelo on Saturday evening in what will be their first-ever encounter in Portugal's top flight.

The hosts occupy sixth place in the Primeira Liga table, eight points and five positions ahead of their visitors, who are four points above the relegation play-off spot.

Academico de Viseu have made an encouraging return to the top flight after a 37-year absence, having collected six wins from their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L3), scoring 15 times and conceding 13 at the other end.

Bruno Pinheiro's side, who failed to record a victory in any of their first four outings this term, enjoyed a particularly impressive spell between September 6 and November 1, winning six consecutive league matches, including a famous triumph away to Sporting Lisbon on October 25.

However, that winning run in the top flight came to an end last time out, when the Viseu club suffered a 1-0 defeat to Nacional in Funchal after conceding a late winner to Matchoi Djalo.

The result also means Academico have now alternated between defeats and victories across their last five matches in all competitions, including cup losses to lower-division Fatima in the Taca de Portugal and Primeira Liga champions Porto in the Taca da Liga.

Returning from a three-week hiatus, the Viseu club will be glad to be back at Fontelo, where they have won each of their last three matches, beating Vitoria de Guimaraes, Estoril Praia and Rio Ave by 2-1 scorelines after losing their opening two fixtures at the ground this term.

Like the hosts, Alverca also started the campaign slowly, failing to record a victory in any of their opening five fixtures, but enjoyed a three-match winning run between September 12 and October 12, beating Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao.

However, the Ribatejo club have slipped back into familiar struggles, having since gone winless in four matches across all competitions, starting with a Taca de Portugal elimination at the hands of second-tier Tondela before suffering narrow league defeats against Arouca and Benfica.

Sergio Ferreira's team then drew 1-1 with Casa Pia in their most recent outing, with Ian Luccas finding the net in the 66th minute to rescue a point, while the goal ended a three-match run without scoring.

Two wins from their last three league games on the road suggest Alverca have also held their own away from home, although they have been vulnerable when not at their best, losing three of their five away league outings this season.

There is also little to draw from history, given the Ribatejo club are without a victory in their previous three meetings with Academico, losing twice in that spell, although their most recent visit to Viseu ended in a 2-2 draw in February 2025 in Liga 2.

With no reported injury or suspension concerns, Academico head coach Pinheiro could retain a similar lineup to the one that featured against Nacional, with goalkeeper Ewerton shielded by the defensive quartet of Anthony Correia, Nikolaos Michelis, Robinho and Miguel Angel Brau.

Andre Clovis has scored five of the Viseu club's 15 league goals this season and also provided an assist, with the Brazilian expected to lead the line here.

Alverca could be without Rayan Lucas, who remains a doubt after suffering another setback with his left knee, although the midfielder has returned to integrated training.

Nabil Touaizi is also expected to miss out after suffering a relapse of a right-calf injury, while Bastien Meupiyou and Sabit Abdulai remain sidelined following knee surgery.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Noah Raveyre is another absentee, with his return expected in early December.

Academico de Viseu possible starting lineup:.

Ewerton; Robinho, Correia, Michelis, Brau; L Silva, Messeguem; Guilherme, Kahraman, Mortimer; Clovis.

Alverca possible starting lineup:.

Mendes; Boyan, Gomez, James; Spencer, I Luccas, Gui, Chissumba; Chiquinho, Camara, Figueiredo.

Academico have struggled to find the net in recent weeks, but their overall league form and stronger position in the table make them worthy favourites against an Alverca side that have scored just once in their last four matches, so a home victory looks plausible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 20:55.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has declined to discuss the potential return of Nico Paz to the Santiago Bernabeu amid conflicting reports in Spain over the club's intention to activate their £68m buy-back option for the Como midfielder.

The Argentina international continues to impress in Italian football, registering six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as one of Europe's most exciting young attacking midfielders.

According to recent reports, madrid retained the option to bring Paz back in the summer of 2027 when an agreement was reached with Como in June to allow the 22-year-old to continue his development in Serie A. However, despite recent suggestions that the Spanish giants have already decided to exercise that option, uncertainty remains over their plans.

Asked about Paz during his press conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, Mourinho offered a typically brief response: "He's not my player.".

The Portuguese manager's reluctance to discuss a player contracted to another club should not be interpreted as opposition to the transfer, although his response offered little clarification following contrasting reports in the Spanish media.

Cadena COPE reported last week that Real Madrid intended to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option next summer, with Como having reportedly been informed of the decision.

However, according to Jose Felix Diaz of AS, Madrid have yet to reach a definitive conclusion and could wait until the spring before deciding whether to bring their former academy prospect back.

The club's official statement in June confirmed the existence of a unilateral buy-back option for the 2027-28 season. Crucially, the agreement allowing Paz to remain in Italy for another year was reached at the player's own request, underlining the importance he attaches to regular first-team football at this stage of his career.

The biggest sporting consideration for Madrid remains the presence of Jude Bellingham, whose performances under Mourinho have strengthened his position as the team's principal attacking midfielder.

The England international has scored seven goals and provided five assists in 18 appearances this season, including a goal and an assist in Tuesday's 5-1 victory over PSV. Madrid are also reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new contract for Bellingham, whose existing agreement runs until 2029.

Sources indicate that paz's versatility would give Mourinho some scope to accommodate both players. The Argentine is capable of operating from the right or in a slightly deeper midfield position, although those roles would bring him into direct competition with Arda Guler, Brahim Diaz and Bernardo Silva.

Madrid must also consider how the squad will look next season, with Rodrygo expected to return from injury and Franco Mastantuono due back from his loan spell. Summer signing Yan Diomande represents another significant investment in the attacking department.

Sources indicate that spending £68m on Paz could still make considerable financial sense given his age, development and potential resale value. However, the circumstances that prompted him to remain at Como last summer have hardly changed, particularly with Bellingham enjoying such an influential role under Mourinho.

Waiting until the spring would allow Madrid to assess both Paz's progress and the needs of their own squad before committing to a substantial expenditure. With their final buy-back opportunity approaching, the Spanish giants must determine whether they can offer the Argentine the regular football that has allowed him to flourish in Italy.

Published: 13:30 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 13:30 EST, 25 November 2026.

An English soccer star has been killed outside a Mississippi taco restaurant just months after moving to the United States to chase his dreams.

According to recent reports, krissh Mahatma, 18, was fatally struck by a bullet after a gun was fired outside the Green Ghost Tacos restaurant in Jackson at around 3:39 a.m. on Sunday morning.

The London-born player was with teammates from his Co-Lin Wolves team when they came across a drunk man outside the restaurant, according to Dark Horse Press.

A fight broke out and a man pulled out a gun and fired into the group, hitting Mahatma, who was taken to a nearby hospital via a private vehicle where he died, according to Hinds County Coroner Jeramiah Howard, via WLBT.

According to recent reports, capitol Police have since arrested and charged Danny Luna, 22, with murder. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety did not elaborate on what caused the deadly confrontation.

'While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognize that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one,' Police Chief Mark Miller said, sending 'thoughts and prayers' to Mahatma's 'family and loved ones.'.

Mahatma, who played as a striker, was in his freshman year at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Wesson, around 45 miles south of Jackson where the incident took place.

Krissh Mahatma, 18, was fatally shot outside a taco restaurant in Jackson, Mississippi.

Danny Luna, 22, has been arrested and charged with murder after the deadly confrontation.

He had made 14 appearances in his first three months with the Co-Lin Wolves, scoring one goal in September in a 3-2 win over National Park College.

Sources indicate that 'Copiah-Lincoln Community College is mourning the loss of freshman soccer player Krissh Mahatma. Krissh will be deeply missed by his teammates and the entire Co-Lin family,' Dewayne Middleton, the Co-Lin president, said in a statement.

According to recent reports, before moving to the US, he had played for Watford 'A' in the post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league. Co-Lin announced his signing in February.

A fundraiser set up to support his family said he was 'just beginning a new chapter of life far away from home' and added: 'his sudden passing has left his family, friends, teammates, coaches, and the entire Co-Lin soccer community heartbroken.

'Behind this tragedy is a family grieving the loss of their son and loved ones trying to make sense of a loss that feels impossible to put into words.'.

The owner of the Green Ghost Tacos eatery noted: 'On behalf of the entire Green Ghost family, I extend my deepest and most heartfelt condolences to the family, friends, loved ones, and university community mourning the tragic loss of a young student. Our hearts are heavy, and our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by this devastating incident.

'While this tragedy occurred near our establishment, we would like to clarify that Green Ghost was closed and was not conducting business at the time of the shooting.

'The safety and well-being of our patrons, employees, and surrounding community remain a top priority. We are committed to cooperating fully with law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident.

'Out of respect for the grieving family and the investigation, we will refrain from speculating or commenting further on the details at this time.

Recent findings suggest that 'Above all, we recognize that a family has suffered an unimaginable loss. We ask that the community join us in extending compassion, prayers, and support to those affected during this incredibly difficult time.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • Industry observers note that "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

Industry observers note that "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Sources indicate that names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

"A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

Sources indicate that but a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, shows how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

In a recent development, names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer said their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

Industry observers note that research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

"Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

In a recent development, even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

Pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

"People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

Industry observers note that later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she remarked.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Industry observers note that tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

But the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

Recent findings suggest that "I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

It has been revealed that but Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum said.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

In a recent development, that does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

Industry observers note that pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

McKennie indicates USA players could follow Pochettino to Manchester United

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, weston McKennie has mentioned USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there.
  • It has been revealed that the question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford.
  • Sources indicate that mcKennie called the speculation inevitable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, weston McKennie has mentioned USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

It has been revealed that the question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

Sources indicate that mcKennie called the speculation inevitable. He noted many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

Pochettino was asked about the same subject. He mentioned now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

In a recent development, pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

In a recent development, the comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s aims and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

According to recent reports, his contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

In a recent development, mcKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

It has been revealed that the club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

According to recent reports, losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

According to recent reports, mcKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

Sources indicate that the next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 21:01.

In a recent development, vitoria de Guimaraes will look to end a three-match winless run across all competitions when they welcome Estrela Amadora to Estadio D. Afonso Henriques on Saturday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the Primeira Liga table with nine points from 11 matches, just one point and two places behind the visitors, whose early-season resilience has begun to fade.

Vitoria endured their lowest league finish in eight years last term, ending the campaign in ninth place, and their efforts to climb back towards the higher reaches of the table this season have so far proved difficult.

Closer to the relegation zone than the European places, Tiago Margarido's side sit just one point above the relegation playoff spot and 11 behind fifth-placed Arouca, having managed only two wins from their opening 11 league matches (D3, L6).

With victories proving hard to come by, Vitoria have won just one of their eight league games (D3, L4) since beating Nacional on matchday three, with their most recent triumph coming in a 5-0 thrashing of Maritimo on October 23.

Margarido's side have since played out a goalless draw with Gil Vicente before suffering a 2-1 defeat to leaders Porto in their latest top-flight outing, leaving the Guimaraes club with 11 goals scored and 12 conceded in the league this season.

Vitoria suffered another setback at the weekend, when they were eliminated from the Taca de Portugal following a 2-0 defeat to Braga, meaning they have now lost consecutive matches at D. Afonso Henriques for the first time since December 2025.

Meanwhile, the Conquerors have collected eight points from six league matches (W2, D2, L2) at the Minho ground this season and will be looking to improve that tally with a positive result on Saturday.

Estrela, on the other hand, have seen their solid start to the campaign under manager Pepa fade, having now lost each of their last five league matches following an unbeaten run across their opening six fixtures.

While defeats to Academico, Arouca and Casa Pia were disappointing, the Tricolores' two most recent losses have been particularly painful, as they conceded stoppage-time winners in a 2-1 defeat to Moreirense and a 3-2 setback against Benfica.

As a result, Estrela have conceded at least twice in nine of their 11 league matches this season and shipped a total of 22 goals in the Primeira Liga campaign, with only Rio Ave (24) allowing more, while the Amadora club have scored 17 at the other end.

However, there was some encouragement in their most recent outing, as the Tricolores defeated Portimonense 1-0 in the Taca de Portugal to secure a place in the last 16 and record their first clean sheet in 13 matches.

While Estrela will look to build on that cup success, they have a poor away record to contend with heading into the weekend, having managed just one league victory in 14 away games this year (D5, L8).

The visitors have also struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last six league encounters and losing five, including a 2-1 defeat at D. Afonso Henriques in February.

The hosts have also suffered a major setback at left-back, as Joao Mendes has been ruled out for the rest of the season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury to his right knee, while backup Francisco Dias is also unavailable with a right foot sprain.

As a result, Tomas Rodrigues has been called up from the B team to provide cover on the left, although Mohammed Kebdani could feature there, while goalkeeper Juan Castillo has returned to training after an ankle injury but Lucas Furtado is expected to retain his place between the sticks.

Estrela have no reported suspensions, while Jeremy Arevalo is a doubt with a back problem that has prevented him from featuring for the Tricolores since joining from Stuttgart in the summer.

Eddy Doue and Beni Souza have been left out of recent squads for disciplinary reasons and remain doubts for Saturday's trip to Guimaraes.

Leandro Antonetti ended a six-match league goal drought by scoring against Benfica and right now leads the team with five Primeira Liga goals this season, a tally he will be looking to add to this weekend.

Ian Stoica also scored his first goal in seven matches with the winner against Portimonense in the domestic cup and will be keen to find greater consistency in front of goal.

SC Paderborn's clash with visitors Schalke 04 on Saturday at Home Deluxe Arena will be crucial in the Bundesliga's relegation battle.

Sitting 15th with 10 points, the hosts are only above 16th-placed Schalke by three points, and a defeat could leave them as low as 17th by the end of matchweek 11.

The relegation battle looks set to be intense, as while last-placed Borussia Monchengladbach are stranded in 18th, only three points separate 17th from 13th.

Paderborn are one place above the league's relegation playoff spot following their 4-0 loss against Bayer Leverkusen on November 21.

That was their first defeat in five Bundesliga games, though the club drew three times in that period, with their only triumph a 1-0 win against Hamburger SV on October 24.

The hosts have failed to score in three of their last four games in all competitions, and they conceded as many goals in their past two clashes (six) as they had in their prior six contests.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will be pleased by his side's home record given they have won two of their five top-flight fixtures at Home Deluxe Arena while only being beaten twice.

Schalke could view their goalless stalemate with Stuttgart on November 21 positively, especially as it arrested a four-match losing streak.

However, it would be understandable if boss Miron Muslic was feeling pressure given he has failed to oversee a victory in eight games, with his side losing on five occasions.

Industry observers note that the visitors might take comfort from the fact they have beaten their hosts in their two most recent meetings, the latest of which was a 3-2 success in the 2. Bundesliga in April 2026.

Die Knappen rank 18th in the division for goals scored (five), though only Borussia Dortmund (seven), Bayern Munich (10) and Freiburg (10) have conceded fewer times (11).

Schalke's form on the road has been poor considering they are winless in their last four away outings, suffering three losses.

Paderborn will be unable to call upon defenders Marcel Hoffmeier (muscle) and Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant (ankle), as well as forward Timur Gayret (knee).

Jano ter Horst, Tjark Scheller and Mattes Hansen have been regulars in the backline, and they are set to protect goalkeeper Nahuel Noll.

Stefano Marino and Marvin Pieringer are likely to be trusted as a front two, and they will be keen to improve upon their tallies of two and one league goal respectively.

Schalke's absentee list is extensive, with defender Timo Becker, midfielder Ron Schallenberg and forward Emil Hojlund three of seven injured stars.

Vitalie Becker will start in the backline, Soufian El-Faouzi is likely to anchor the middle of the pitch and Moussa Sylla is certain to lead the frontline.

Perhaps the most likely outcome is a stalemate, especially as neither have proven to be particularly productive in the final third.

There were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

It has been revealed that the first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

In a recent development, olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

Sources indicate that the trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

Right on the half-hour mark, the home side took the lead. A corner kick from the left was defended awfully in truth, with Pirola getting the better of Diawara in a central area to head off the crossbar, off Maignan and in from six yards out. Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

Industry observers note that milan were inches away from getting themselves level promptly as Pirola turned from the hero in one goalmouth to the hero at the other. Just as it looked like getting out of hand for Milan, Hutchinson scored a goal from nothing. It has been revealed that milan built on the goal that got them back into it, and six minutes later they drew themselves level. Sources indicate that as if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Hutchinson was again the man who did all of the hard work, getting the ball on the touchline and sitting his marker down before driving to the right edge of the box and standing up a cross for Pulisic. Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

With just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays highlighted it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

The finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.
  • Recent findings suggest that it is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture.
  • Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

Recent findings suggest that it is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

"It is very crucial for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra stated.

Elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person.".

The star is also known for speaking out on political issues in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

According to recent reports, this reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra mentioned. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

"And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly.".

Born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist said.

It has been revealed that in Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

Industry observers note that their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more vital following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, in the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they said.

"And I think this is why it's key, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra mentioned. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening.".

It has been revealed that rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra remarked, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

The interview with Hassandra was conducted by Gönna Ketels.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Recent findings suggest that sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know,” Sage stated when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old noted. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman remarked that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he mentioned. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he stated. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

Industry observers note that “It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

Sources indicate that for all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

According to recent reports, sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

In a recent development, three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

Sources indicate that “It’s not my decision,” Sage mentioned. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

According to recent reports, with only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

According to recent reports, all Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

Recent findings suggest that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

According to recent reports, brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German mentioned: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.
